proposed_statement_changes.proposed: There is a constant \(c_{\star}>0\) such that, uniformly in the allowed designs and \(p,u\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\), \(\inf_{b,b'\in\mathbb R}\|a\mathbf 1+bq_N(p)-b'q_N(u)\|\ge c_{\star}|a|\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R\). On the diagonal the tangent version is \(\inf_{b,c\in\mathbb R}\|a\mathbf1+bq_N(p)+cq_N'(p)\|\ge c_{\star}|a|\). For the ideal curve \(v(p)=(1,t,t^2)^{\mathsf T}\), where \(t=2^{2p-1}\), and a second exponent \(u\) with \(r=2^{2u-1}\), the normal vector is \((tr,-t-r,1)^{\mathsf T}\); it annihilates \(v(p)\) and \(v(u)\) and its inner product with \(\mathbf1\) is \((t-1)(r-1)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen ideal-curve sentence reuses \(u\) both as an exponent and as the geometric ratio. With \(u\) interpreted as the exponent, \((tu,-t-u,1)\) does not annihilate \(q_N(u)\). The corrected claim names the required ratio \(r=2^{2u-1}\) and writes the diagonal tangent inequality explicitly; the substantive uniform separation claim is unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(d=1\), \(D=[0,1]\), the sites are equally spaced, the stencil radii are integer lattice multiples, and \(|\mathcal G_{N,j}|/N\to\eta_j>0\), the affine-stencil construction satisfies \(q_N(p)\to(1,2^{2p-1},4^{2p-1})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(H_N\to\operatorname{diag}(\eta_0^{-1},\eta_1^{-1},\eta_2^{-1})\). In particular, if the balanced construction has common limiting stencil fraction \(\eta\), then \(H_N\to\eta^{-1}I_3\). The profile construction remains nonsingular at \(A=0\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen covariance matrix \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&2\\1&2&4\end{psmallmatrix}\) is the nested first-increment matrix, but the frozen algorithm uses spatially separated affine-annihilating second-difference stencils. On a one-dimensional lattice, the principal kernel \(|x-y|\) is affine across disjoint support intervals, so \(R_{N,ab}=0\) for distinct stencils and the stated \(H_N\) is diagonal. The proposed conclusion is the exact specialization of the actual frozen construction.

proposed.name: ghat
proposed.def: Let \(\underline c_X\) and \(\overline c_X\) be the minimum and maximum of the \(c_X\)-projection of \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nuis}}\), and define \(\underline c_W,\overline c_W\) analogously. With \(\operatorname{clip}_{[l,u]}(x)=\min\{u,\max\{l,x\}\}\), set \(\widehat\gamma_N=\operatorname{clip}_{[\underline c_W/2,2\overline c_W]}(\widehat c_W)/\operatorname{clip}_{[\underline c_X/2,2\overline c_X]}(\widehat c_X)\).
proposed.role: feasible scale ratio with explicit deterministic clipping

proposed_core_edits.reason: The frozen notation uses an unspecified clipping map. Explicit intervals containing the compact scale projections are required for consistency, positivity, and the pathwise expected-diameter bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform anti-concentration and quantile-attainment theorem for \(d_{H_N}(G_N+\lambda q_N(p),\mathcal C_N)^2\) over bounded local amplitudes, \(|\lambda|\to\infty\), exponent endpoints, and nonconvergent allowed design sequences, together with a certified one-sided numerical approximation of the resulting attainable supremum quantile.
open_obligations.obstruction: Bounded-Lipschitz convergence alone does not control probabilities at a changing family of profile boundaries. The diverging-amplitude limits change from tangent planes in the exponent interior to one-sided tangent half-planes at the endpoints, and the frozen assumptions provide neither the required uniform anti-concentration modulus nor a computable representation of the nuisance compactum sufficient for interval certification.
open_obligations.attempted: Compactify the uniformly bounded \(C^1\) curves and positive-definite matrices; use Gaussian tube continuity for bounded \(\lambda\); rescale \(p-p_0\) by \(|\lambda|\) for tangent-plane and endpoint half-plane limits; and define the critical value as the supremum of attainable Gaussian quantiles. These steps establish the candidate limit families but do not prove a uniform continuity modulus across their junctions or certified continuum optimization from the stated primitives.
